goal: Decide whether talata adds an HTML output identical to micromark(value, {extensions: [gfm()], htmlExtensions: [gfmHtml()]}), or keeps HTML as a non-goal

extra_axes.name: scope
extra_axes.why: the user's stated idea is 'faster micromark'; HTML output decides whether talata matches that idea
extra_axes.ruling_why: the decision is about what talata replaces, which no device, time or token number settles

claims.text: talata's existing path (fromMarkdown, mdast-util-to-hast, hast-util-to-html) renders HTML 6.5x faster than micromark HTML + GFM on the READMEs and 7.5x on node fs.md.
That path gives the same HTML string as micromark for 1 of 139 READMEs (6 of 139 ignoring blank lines), so it is not a drop-in for micromark() callers.

micromark has 58.1M weekly downloads and mdast-util-from-markdown 56.5M, so at most about 1.6M a week (3%) reach micromark other than through mdast-util-from-markdown. Direct HTML callers are a subset of that.

micromark-baseline/README.md, the origin of the idea, defines it as a rewrite of micromark and mdast-util-from-markdown that passes the same spec tests and produces the same mdast while parsing faster. HTML appears only as a baseline row.

Add talata/html: toHtml(value, {gfm}) that returns the same HTML string as micromark with gfm and gfmHtml, built straight from talata's parse without an mdast tree, so talata is a full faster micromark.

estimate.unit: x faster than micromark html (guess, near parse-only speed)

evidence.source: J1: parse alone is 16.2x to 18.2x; a direct renderer skips to-hast and to-html

claims.ruling_why: J3 and J4: the replaced thing is mdast-util-from-markdown, and at most 3% of micromark's reach is direct; J1 shows HTML users already get 6.5x to 7.5x today.

claims.text: Test it cheaply: the CommonMark and GFM spec examples are HTML, and micromark passes all 652, so the existing harness and fuzzer can compare HTML strings.

Keep HTML a non-goal for 0.1. Document the to-hast path in the README with its measured speed and the note that its HTML differs from micromark's. Park a byte-identical talata/html as an outline node, revisited when users ask for it after 0.1.

A second output with a byte-exact contract against micromark's HTML (attribute order, escaping, footnote sections, raw HTML handling, line endings) is a second release-blocking differential target: new renderer, fuzzer mode, spec harness mode. It delays 0.1 by about one L node.

evidence.source: roadmaps/CALIBRATION.md: gfm-green and spec-green were S to L with several fuzz rounds each

claims.text: A renderer and its GFM parts add code to the bundle. The browser margin over the reference is about 1.4 KB gzip, but a separate talata/html entry would not reach users of the main entry.
HTML output pulls toward HTML-only extensions (micromark htmlExtensions), a second extension surface that the extension plan in GOAL.md does not cover.
Spec examples are normalized HTML, while micromark callers depend on exact output, so spec passes do not prove byte equality on real documents; the fuzzer would still need an HTML mode.
